title: String Quartet in G minor
hook: One short theme, four movements, four new disguises, and the first chamber work of a new century of sound.

painting.title: Rouen Cathedral, West Façade, Sunlight
painting.pairingNote: Painted in the same years as the quartet, one of more than thirty views of the same façade, each in a different light; Debussy does the same with one theme, seen four times in a new colour.

facts: Debussy wrote the quartet in 1892–93, when he was 31 and still little known, in the same years as his *Prélude à l’après-midi d’un faune*. It is his only string quartet, and the only work he ever published with an opus number.

He meant to dedicate it to his friend and fellow composer Ernest Chausson, who had reservations about it. Debussy began a second quartet to answer his doubts, but their friendship broke off and the second quartet was never finished.

The Ysaÿe Quartet, led by the Belgian violinist Eugène Ysaÿe, gave the first performance at a concert of the Société nationale de musique in Paris on 29 December 1893. The reaction was mixed: one Belgian critic called it more of a hallucination than a dream.

The whole work grows from one short theme. It opens the first movement, drives the second, is hinted at in the third and returns, transformed, in the finale. This is [[cyclic-form|cyclic form]], a technique associated with César Franck and his circle, but the harmonies, the old church scales and the play of colour are entirely his own.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a bold theme (I), the same theme plucked and dancing (II), a muted dream (III), a slow awakening that ends in a rush of energy (IV).

movements.heading: Animé et très décidé
movements.summary: All four instruments launch the theme together, forcefully, with a quick little turn in it. The theme uses an old church scale, so it sounds both ancient and strange. The movement follows [[sonata-form|sonata form]] loosely: a second, gentler melody, a restless middle where the theme is broken up and passed around, and a return of the opening before a vigorous close.

mainIdeas.name: The theme
mainIdeas.description: short and decisive, with a quick turn in the middle, played by all four together. Everything in the quartet comes from it.

mainIdeas.name: The second melody
mainIdeas.description: a long, singing line in the first violin, softer and warmer.

notice: Learn the opening theme well, especially its quick turn. You will hear it again in every movement, sometimes very well disguised.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: The young French Quatuor Ébène recorded the quartet in February 2008, together with the quartets of Fauré and Ravel, for their first album on Virgin Classics. It was named Gramophone’s Recording of the Year in 2009. On the Spotify album the Debussy is tracks 1–4.

movements.heading: Assez vif et bien rythmé
movements.summary: The scherzo. The viola plays the main theme again and again, bowed and stubborn, while the other three pluck around it in shifting, off-beat patterns. In the middle the bows come back and the theme is stretched into a long, singing line. Then the plucking returns. Manuel de Falla heard in this movement one of the most beautiful Andalusian dances ever written.

mainIdeas.description: The theme from the first movement, reshaped by the viola into a short, repeated figure, an [[ostinato|ostinato]].

mainIdeas.name: The plucked accompaniment
mainIdeas.description: [[pizzicato|pizzicato]] chords and rhythms that pull against the beat, like a guitar.

stops.hear: The others pluck sharp chords; the viola plays a short tune over and over
stops.happening: The first movement’s theme, now a dance

stops.hear: Plucked notes fly between all four instruments in tangled, off-beat rhythms
stops.happening: Rhythms that cut across the beat

stops.hear: The bows return; the first violin plays the theme stretched into a long, smooth melody
The plucking starts again, and the theme returns to the lower instruments

stops.label: Last 15 seconds
stops.hear: A light, quiet flurry of plucked notes, and it is gone

notice: Listen to the viola at the start, then to how the plucked chords keep landing in unexpected places. The quartet sounds like a single, many-stringed guitar.

movements.heading: Andantino, doucement expressif
movements.summary: The slow movement, played with [[muted|muted]] strings for most of its length. It is the most intimate music in the quartet: soft, slow melodies in a warm, distant key, with a more passionate middle section that begins with the viola alone. The first movement’s theme is only hinted at. Then the mutes return and the music fades into silence.

mainIdeas.name: The opening melody
mainIdeas.description: slow and veiled, rising and falling gently over soft, close harmonies.

mainIdeas.name: The viola’s melody
mainIdeas.description: a longer, more searching line that starts the middle section.

stops.hear: Very soft, veiled strings play a slow, gentle melody
stops.happening: The muted opening, in D-flat major

stops.hear: The melody passes to the lower instruments and the harmony deepens
stops.happening: The tune spreads through the quartet

stops.hear: The viola alone begins a new, more searching melody; the others join one by one
The music grows louder and more intense, the instruments climbing together
The opening melody returns, soft and veiled again

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: High, very quiet chords that thin out into silence

notice: The mutes take the brightness off the sound. Notice how the music changes colour when they come off for the climax, and when they go back on.

movements.heading: Très modéré – Très mouvementé et avec passion
movements.tempo: Très modéré – Très mouvementé et avec passion
movements.summary: The finale starts slowly, almost groping in the dark, with fragments that recall the slow movement and the theme from the start. The pace gathers until the music breaks into a fast, passionate main section. The theme returns in many new shapes, and at the end it bursts out bright and fast, as a whirlwind close.

mainIdeas.name: The slow introduction
mainIdeas.description: low, searching lines that gradually speed up.

mainIdeas.name: The fast music
mainIdeas.description: a restless, driving idea built from the opening theme.

mainIdeas.name: The theme’s last disguise
mainIdeas.description: fast, bright and in a major key, at the very end.

threads.title: One theme, many shapes
threads.body: The same short theme opens the work, dances in the scherzo, is hinted at in the slow movement and blazes out at the end.

threads.title: Four voices as an orchestra
threads.body: Plucking, muting, rapid tremolos and close, rich chords give the quartet a range of colours that sounds larger than four instruments.

threads.title: Old scales, new harmonies
threads.body: Debussy borrows church modes and harmonies that move freely, without the usual pull towards home. Critics in 1893 were puzzled; ten years later Ravel modelled his own quartet on this one.
